subject: Andrew's proposal for avoiding model recompilation

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Andrew's proposal for avoiding model recompilation
parts:
Here's Andrew's proposal for avoiding model recompilation,
as far as I understood it:

1. Each call to RStan's stan() function will be supplied with:
-- a model name
-- the model contents as a string or file
-- a working directory into which results are written

2. The model contents get written to the working directory
in a file given by the model name.

3. When a model's (re)compiled, we save (in some space private
to RStan that won't get overwritten by users):
-- the name of the model,
-- the working directory

4. We only compile the model if:
-- there is no compiled model loaded at the time, or
-- there is a compiled model loaded, but
* the name of model is different,
* the working directory location is different, or
* the contents saved in the working directory don't match
the about-to-be-compiled model contents

This should work. (Having named directories and named models is
what I was talking about when I said we'd have to deal with
some naming conventions.)

As I understand it from Jiqiang, there's no good way to save the
shared object (.so) or dynamic linked lib (.dll) across R sessions.
So it'll have to be compiled at least once per session.

It does mean that we won't be able to bounce back and forth
among different models. So if you run eight schools, then
speed dating in the same R session, you'll have to compile eight
schools again the next time you use it. A more general way of
doing this might be to create a stack of model names/working dirs
in R's memory, but that would require being able to reload the
models. Is that possible?

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Andrew's proposal for avoiding model recompilation
parts:
This is a bit complicated.  I propose we just maintain a table in the R's working space.  In the table, we just have columns such as

ID, stanmodel 

I suppose we can create an ID from a character string of Stan model code using some hash algorithm.  After a model compiling is potentially needed, we use the ID to see if we have already compiled the model.  If yes, we just use the table to obtain the stanmodel that was compiled previously.  If no, we compile the model and put the compiled the stanmodel in the table.  I do not see a problem if we first fit a 8 schools model, then a rats model, then 8 schools again.  One issue I see now is that R allows user to delete objects and R's garbage collector could delete objects if they are used anymore, in which case I am not sure it is possible to delete records from the table.

As I understand it from Jiqiang, there's no good way to save the
shared object (.so) or dynamic linked lib (.dll) across R sessions.
So it'll have to be compiled at least once per session.

Yes. All works fine just in one session.  The programmer of rstan knows the same about those shared objects as the user of rstan. We delegate the compiling of C++ code to package inline, so we do not where they are saved and when/how they loaded though we might be able to get those information if we want.  And this is the reason why we have problems with saving compiled models and reloading them.

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 6ad178c9bfa534b7
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Andrew's proposal for avoiding model recompilation
parts:
If you just need the objects accessible for the session, I think you can do this with a couple lines of code using the package memoise. When you memoise a function it will cache the results for each unique input a function is called with, and when the function is called again with those same inputs it will return the cached results.  I prototyped it with cxxfunction and basic examples and it seems to work.  In the example below, it will only compile the code the first time.  The second time it immediately returns the function. 

library(memoise)
library(RcppArmadillo)
## Original function
compilefun <- function(sig, body, plugin) {
    cxxfunction(sig, body, plugin = plugin, verbose=TRUE)
}
## Memoised function
smartcompile <- memoise(compilefun)
 
sig1 <- signature(x="integer", y="numeric")
body1 <- 'return ScalarReal( INTEGER(x)[0] * REAL(y)[0] ) ;'
 
f1 <- smartcompile(sig1, body1, "default")
f2 <- smartcompile(sig1, body1, "default")
identical(f1, f2)
 
sig2 <- sig1
body2 <- 'return wrap( as<int>(x) * as<double>(y) ) ;'
f3 <- smartcompile(sig2, body2, "Rcpp")
f4 <- smartcompile(sig2, body2, "Rcpp")
identical(f3, f4)

To persist objects across sessions, once the inline problem is figured out, is a lot like how the packages knitr or cacher persist the results of evaluating chunks of code, and their caching systems can probably be heavily borrowed from.

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Andrew's proposal for avoiding model recompilation
parts:
As a suggestion which might allow things to persist across sessions why don't you use a tmp directory?  For instance, when stan() is called the directory $TMPDIR/RStan-$USERNAME/<md5sum of model contents>/ is created if it doesn't exist and is used to hold all information.  If it already exists it can be assumed that the contents corresponds to the same model.  The md5sum of the model contents ensures that if the filename or model name remains the same but the model is changed (as might happen when people are tweaking a model) it still gets recompiled.

In other words, instead of creating a table in R, you use the filesystem temp directory as a table.

Cheers,
Marcus

On 8/14/12 11:30 AM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> Bob
> I'm not disputing you on this--you know how the computer works
> and I don't--but I'm confused.
This is an R inline package issue.

> Why can't we simply, after
> compiling a model, save the object code as an object (or as
> a file if it's not possible to save as an object)

I'm not sure what you mean by "save the object code as
an object". Save it where? Once the dynamically compiled
model binary is loaded, we'll save a reference (link, pointer)
to it. So we'll be able to refetch within the same session
no problem. (This wouldn't be the case if inline always loaded
the same object code name -- I don't know how it generates
the name of the dynamic binary (.so or .dll) to load.)

The dynamic object file (.so or .dll) will be stored in
a file (I don't think there's a way to get around that) by
the inline package. Jiqiang said the problem is that they
don't tell us where it is saved. We could certainly figure
this out for one platform assuming it's not randomized in some
crazy way (you never know what people will do to try to avoid
name conflicts). And maybe we could reload it next time.

> and then just
> access it later if needed. If we do schools, then speed dating,
> then schools, why can't the second run of schools just access the already-created object code?

That's exactly what we're talking about doing for
runs within a single session of R. The problem again
is how objects and state get saved in R. The dynamic
libraries aren't saved and reloaded when you reload
R.

- Bob
